issues.description: Constructors for Animal and its concrete subclasses: The problem statement (UML and example Main) indicates Animal has only a 'name' attribute and the example Main constructs animals with a single String argument (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). The solution repository, however, adds an 'age' attribute to Animal and defines constructors that require two parameters (String name, int age) in Animal and in Seal, Pig, and Goat. This inconsistency means code or tests that follow the problem/template (single-argument constructors) will not compile against the solution constructors, and students following the template Main will be confused or get compilation errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred for minimal changes): remove the extra 'age' attribute from the solution's Animal class and change Animal, Seal, Pig, and Goat constructors to accept only (String name), updating their super(...) calls accordingly so they match the UML and the template Main examples. Option B: if 'age' is intended as required, update the problem statement (UML and textual description) and the template Main examples to require and show the two-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", 3)), and update the UML to include the 'age' attribute. Ensure tests, UML, template code, and solution constructors all use the same parameter list.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for Animal and its subclasses: the problem description (UML and instructions) and the template Main example show single-argument constructors that accept only a name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")). The solution repository instead defines Animal and subclass constructors that require two parameters (Animal(String name, int age); Seal(String name, int age); Pig(String name, int age); Goat(String name, int age)). The UML in the problem statement declares only a name attribute for Animal. This inconsistency means student code following the problem statement or template Main will not compile against the solution API and creates confusion about the required constructor parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor parameters consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: add single-argument constructors for backward compatibility to the solution—e.g., add Animal(String name) (or Animal(String name) delegating to Animal(String name, int age) with a default age) and corresponding one-argument constructors in Seal, Pig, Goat that call super(name). Alternatively, update the problem statement and template Main to show and require two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and document the additional 'age' attribute. Ensure the UML, example Main, and solution constructors all present the same constructor signatures.
